about: The explainer's narration, one line per step. narrate.py voices them into audio/step-N.mp3, which the explainer plays when its sound is on.

lines.text: stretto-proxy wraps any MCP server. The host runs it in place of the server's command, and it forwards every message both ways, unchanged. The agent keeps its prompt and its tools. Until you give the proxy a flow, it only forwards and records.

Use the agent as usual. The proxy writes each session to a log: the calls, their results, and the conversation if the host shares it. The logs are all a flow learns from, so record the kinds of request the agent will see. In replay, ten of an agent's own sessions gave over 90% of what all of them did.

stretto learn counts which reads followed which calls, and where each read's arguments came from: here, the order numbers in the user's record. The result is a flow, a file you review like code, with flow-show and flow-diff.

Served, the flow runs after each of the agent's calls. It makes the lookups the agent is likely to need, with arguments bound from the results so far, and they ride in the same tool result. The agent has them before it would ask, so it spends fewer LLM turns. Run a flow in shadow first, then promote the sites whose lookups were the agent's own.

A detour is a lookup the agent did not use. Its result stays in the context, so every later LLM turn reads it again: that is its cost, in tokens. It cannot change the state, since a flow only reads. Live, a detour carried about 2,530 input tokens, and a saved turn saved about 6,000.

The reach decider asks no model and needs no key. It makes a lookup when the chance that the agent uses it before its next write clears a threshold set by those costs, about 0.3. That chance, not the chance the read comes next, is the one that pays: the agent may reply first, and still read it before it writes.

Live, with GLM-5.3 as agent and user on 28 τ²-bench retail and airline tasks, stretto took 27.9% fewer LLM turns, and input tokens fell 21.9%. Passes went from 24 to 21, which 28 tasks cannot tell from the agent's own variance. In AgentDojo's Slack and travel suites, GLM-5.3 and Claude Haiku 4.5 took 10.1% fewer turns, with passes unchanged. In BFCL there was no effect.
